newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton, Yeltsin optimistic on summit talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin optimistic on summit talks.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin expressed optimism as they began summit talks on Friday, although Yeltsin said he was still not convinced NATO enlargement was a good idea.
"I think we'll have a good meeting," Clinton told reporters at the summit venue, Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari's official residence overlooking the still-frozen Baltic Sea.
The Russian president said: "I think both sides are ready to meet each other and, through compromise, to resolve the problems and disagreements."
Yeltsin was asked by reporters whether he now accepted the U.S. and Western argument that NATO enlargement posed no threat to Russia. He replied, "I have not been convinced otherwise."
The Kremlin chief said the two men had prepared the ground for the talks -- which will focus on NATO expansion, arms control and economic issues -- with their good-humoured dinner on Thursday.
"Yesterday, we warmed each other up so that today there won't be such tension at the negotiation," he said.
Clinton refused to answer more questions. The two leaders plan a news conference later on Friday, at around 1645 GMT.
